title: Attune Tenant Impact
description: Generated by go run ./internal/tools/observabilitydash. Do not edit JSON by hand. SLO burn-rate, tenant impact, and attribution for on-call.

panels.title: Tenant impact lens
panels.description: How to read burn-rate and impact.

options.content:
**Targets:** service-owned SLOs burn first; diagnostics stay visible but do not page on their own.

**Flow:** burn trend -> tenant impact -> source / result attribution -> auth, MCP, GDPR, and delivery drilldowns.

**Thresholds:** fast burn > 14.4x · slow burn > 6.0x.

panels.title: Ingest burn x
panels.description: Fast burn multiplier for ingest internal errors and rate-limit pressure. 1x means the budget is being consumed at the planned rate; 14.4x is the classic 30d fast-burn page threshold.

panels.title: Enrich burn x
panels.description: Fast burn multiplier for enrichment attempts that miss the 5s success target. This is the main user-facing latency SLO.

panels.title: Outbox burn x
panels.description: Fast burn multiplier for terminal delivery failures. Pair this with outbox lag to tell destination rejection from worker pressure.

panels.title: OIDC burn x
panels.description: Fast burn multiplier for failed sign-in attempts. This is a service-owned authentication reliability signal.

panels.title: API key burn x
panels.description: Fast burn multiplier for access denials on active API keys. Keep this separate from authz denials so policy-driven rejections stay explainable.

panels.title: MCP burn x
panels.description: Fast burn multiplier for MCP tool-call failures. Use this with tool mix and latency to separate tool regressions from policy pressure.

panels.title: GDPR burn x
panels.description: Fast burn multiplier for GDPR jobs that miss completion. Cancelled and revoked jobs are excluded from the denominator so the lens stays operational.

panels.title: Burn by SLO
panels.description: 5m and 1h burn multipliers for the service-owned SLOs. The fast-burn page threshold is 14.4x; the slow-burn policy uses a lower threshold over a longer window.

panels.title: Tenant burn ranking
panels.description: Current 5m burn multipliers for tenant-scoped SLOs. Use this to answer who is burning budget fastest before opening the detailed SLO pages.

panels.title: Tenant intake and attribution
panels.description: Traffic by source/result plus service-side ingest pressure. This helps separate client schema drift from service regressions.

panels.title: Enrichment and auth pressure
panels.description: Enrichment latency by result and the auth path health signals that often precede Console or API support issues.

panels.title: Delivery pressure
panels.description: Outbox terminal failures, notifier failures, and delivery attempts by destination type. This tells you whether the issue is worker capacity or destination rejection.

panels.title: MCP success %
panels.description: Share of MCP tool calls that returned OK, excluding policy denials and rate limits so tool reliability stays separate from governance pressure.

panels.title: MCP denied %
panels.description: Share of MCP requests denied by policy or throttled by rate limits. High values usually mean governance changes or client misuse.

panels.title: MCP calls
panels.description: Total MCP tool calls in the selected range. Sudden drops usually indicate auth or routing problems before the tool mix changes.

panels.title: MCP p95
panels.description: P95 MCP tool-call latency. Use this with the tool mix panel to tell a slow downstream tool from a general dispatcher slowdown.

targets.expr: ((histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(attune_mcp_tool_latency_seconds_bucket{tenant=~"$tenant"}[$__rate_interval])))) or vector(0)) or vector(0)

panels.title: MCP tool mix
panels.description: MCP tool call rate split by tool and result. This separates tool execution failures from policy denials and throttling.

panels.title: MCP latency by tool
panels.description: MCP latency percentiles by tool. When this rises without a matching error spike, inspect the downstream tool or adapter.

panels.title: GDPR completion %
panels.description: Share of GDPR jobs that completed successfully, excluding intentional cancellations and revocations.

targets.expr: ((sum(rate(attune_gdpr_job_total{tenant=~"$tenant",result="completed"}[$__rate_interval])) / clamp_min(sum(rate(attune_gdpr_job_total{tenant=~"$tenant",result="started"}[$__rate_interval])) - (sum(rate(attune_gdpr_job_total{tenant=~"$tenant",result="cancelled"}[$__rate_interval])) or on(tenant, request_type) (sum(rate(attune_gdpr_job_total{tenant=~"$tenant",result="started"}[$__rate_interval])) * 0)) - (sum(rate(attune_gdpr_job_total{tenant=~"$tenant",result="revoked"}[$__rate_interval])) or on(tenant, request_type) (sum(rate(attune_gdpr_job_total{tenant=~"$tenant",result="started"}[$__rate_interval])) * 0)), 1e-9)) or vector(0)) or vector(0)

panels.title: GDPR failed %
panels.description: Share of GDPR jobs that reached a terminal failure. Spikes usually mean queue, worker, or storage problems.

panels.title: GDPR backlog
panels.description: Approximate outstanding GDPR work in the selected range: started jobs minus terminal jobs. Positive values mean work is not draining.

panels.title: GDPR p95
panels.description: P95 GDPR job duration. Compare this with backlog to tell slow completion from a stalled queue.

targets.expr: ((histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(attune_gdpr_job_duration_seconds_bucket{tenant=~"$tenant"}[$__rate_interval])))) or vector(0)) or vector(0)

panels.title: GDPR state mix
panels.description: GDPR job state mix by request type. Use this to separate export backlog from delete backlog and intentional cancellations.

panels.title: GDPR latency by request
panels.description: GDPR job duration percentiles by request type. Export and delete have different expected shapes, so keep the split visible.

panels.title: Burn history
panels.description: 7d and 30d average burn by SLO. Use this with Burn trend to tell a spike from a sustained regression.

panels.title: Remaining budget
panels.description: Trailing 30d error budget remaining by SLO. Use this with Burn history to tell whether the surface still has room or is already exhausted.

panels.title: Dependency health
panels.description: Upstream dependency check outcomes and latency. Use this to identify whether a service-wide burn is likely coming from a failing dependency before leaving the reliability surface.

panels.title: Routing table
panels.description: Owning area, escalation path, and runbook links for the reliability surface.

panels.title: Replay report
panels.description: Historical outage comparison and backfill worksheet.

options.content:
**Template:** [Open replay report template](https://github.com/Phixsura/attune/blob/main/observability/reports/attune-slo-replay-template.md)

**Use with:** Burn history, Remaining budget, Dependency health, Routing table, and the Comparison matrix.

**Capture:** incident window, dominant tenant, likely dependency, replay lens, and the verdict column.

panels.title: Policy guide
panels.description: Recommended SLO starting point, guardrails, and exception stance.

options.content:
**Template:** [Open policy reference](https://github.com/Phixsura/attune/blob/main/observability/reports/attune-slo-policy-reference.md)

**Use with:** SLO catalog, routing table, replay comparison worksheet, and budget exception register.

**Defaults:** Start from the catalog objective, page at 14.4x on 5m and 1h, warn at 6x on 30m and 6h, keep traffic floors above 0.01, and keep exceptions explicit.
